headline: Massachusetts opens $5 million teacher scholarship round with Nov. 20 deadline
dek: The Tomorrow’s Teachers program offers up to $25,000 a year to eligible students in approved educator-preparation programs, but recipients must complete teaching service in Massachusetts public schools.
body: Massachusetts has opened a new $5 million round of Tomorrow’s Teachers Scholarships for students preparing to become public-school educators, the Healey-Driscoll administration announced Oct. 1. Applications are open through Nov. 20. Eligible students enrolled in approved educator-preparation programs at the state’s public four-year colleges and universities can receive as much as $25,000, subject to available funds and individual eligibility.

The announcement makes the program relevant beyond tuition alone. The state says scholarship money can be used for expenses included in a student’s cost of attendance, including fees, room and board, books and supplies, transportation, child care and personal expenses. That broader definition matters for aspiring teachers who may be balancing coursework with family obligations, commuting or the unpaid and lower-paid portions of professional preparation.

The award is not a no-strings grant. The Massachusetts Office of Student Financial Assistance describes Tomorrow’s Teachers as a repayment-through-service scholarship: one year of teaching forgives one year of scholarship support, while a recipient who does not meet the service obligation can owe the money as a loan. The state’s program rules require recipients to pursue the appropriate Massachusetts teaching credential and become a teacher of record within 12 months after completing a degree or eligible post-baccalaureate coursework. The OSFA program page is available at https://www.mass.edu/osfa/programs/tmwteachers.asp.

For students funded throughout a traditional four-year undergraduate path, the OSFA agreement describes a four-year teaching commitment in a Massachusetts public-school district. Undergraduate students may receive support for up to four years, or eight semesters. Students in approved post-baccalaureate preparation may receive funding for up to three semesters. Those limits mean the headline maximum of $25,000 is an annual ceiling, not a promise that every applicant will receive that amount or that the program will cover every educational cost.

The eligibility rules also narrow the pool. Applicants must generally be Massachusetts residents who meet the state’s citizenship or eligible noncitizen requirements, complete the FAFSA or Massachusetts Application for State Financial Aid, enroll full time in an approved program and meet satisfactory academic progress standards. The public-college list includes Bridgewater State, Fitchburg State, Framingham State, Massachusetts College of Art and Design, Massachusetts College of Liberal Arts, Salem State, Westfield State, Worcester State and the four University of Massachusetts campuses in Amherst, Boston, Dartmouth and Lowell.

The program’s funding sits inside a larger state effort to build an educator pipeline. A June fact sheet from the Massachusetts Legislature says its fiscal 2026 Fair Share supplemental budget provided $10 million for Tomorrow’s Teachers scholarships and loan-forgiveness initiatives; the fact sheet is at https://malegislature.gov/PressRoom/Detail?pressReleaseId=1383. The executive branch’s new announcement identifies $5 million for the scholarship round and says a separate $7,500 loan-repayment component for eligible educators will open applications in April. Those figures describe related pieces of the program, not an additional $5 million available to every scholarship applicant.

The practical effect will depend on who applies, how awards are sized and whether recipients stay in Massachusetts classrooms long enough to satisfy their obligations. The state is presenting the program as a way to reduce the cost of entering teaching and to strengthen and diversify the educator workforce. The available records establish the funding, rules and deadline; they do not yet show how many students will receive awards in this cycle or how many will ultimately enter public-school classrooms.

Prospective applicants should complete the required federal or state financial-aid application, create a MASSAid Student Portal account and review the current OSFA guidelines before submitting a Tomorrow’s Teachers application. The immediate date to watch is Nov. 20. After the application period closes, award counts and the distribution of funding among eligible public colleges will provide the first measure of demand for the new round, while later employment records will show whether the scholarship’s service bargain translates into more licensed teachers in Massachusetts schools.
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoDescription: Massachusetts opened a $5 million Tomorrow’s Teachers scholarship round with applications due Nov. 20 and awards of up to $25,000 a year.
